addresses.33C6: **stk-data** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $34. Puts a number on the stack that is written as 2 to 5 data bytes right after the $34 code in your list. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.33F7: **SKIP-CONS** (ROM routine): Internal helper that steps through the table of constants to find constant number A (0 to 4), leaving its address in HL'.
addresses.3406: **LOC-MEM** (ROM routine): Works out the address of one of the calculator's 5-byte memory slots: returns HL = HL + 5 x A.
addresses.340F: **get-mem** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $E0 to $E5. Copies a number from calculator memory slot 0 to 5 onto the top of the stack. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.341B: **stk-con** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $A0 to $A4. Puts one of the built-in numbers on the stack: $A0 zero, $A1 one, $A2 a half, $A3 half of pi, $A4 ten. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.342D: **st-mem** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $C0 to $C5. Copies the top number into calculator memory slot 0 to 5, leaving it on the stack too. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.343C: **exchange** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $01. Swaps the top two numbers on the calculator stack. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3449: **series** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $86, $88 and $8C. Builds a series of terms from a list of numbers to closely estimate maths functions such as SIN, ATN, LN and EXP. Used by those functions through RST $28.
addresses.346A: **abs** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2A. Makes the top number on the stack positive (removes any minus sign), like ABS in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.346E: **negate** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $1B. Flips the sign of the top number on the stack: plus becomes minus and minus becomes plus. Zero stays zero. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3492: **sgn** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $29. Replaces the top number with 1 if it was positive, 0 if zero, or -1 if negative, like SGN in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.34A5: **in** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2C. Replaces the top number with the byte read from that input port, like IN in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.34AC: **peek** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2B. Replaces the top number (an address) with the byte stored at that address, like PEEK in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.34B3: **usr-no** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2D. Runs machine code at the address given by the top number, like USR in BASIC. Whatever is in BC when your code returns becomes the result.
addresses.34BC: **usr-$** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $19. Handles USR "a" in BASIC: gives the address of the user-defined graphic for a letter a to u. Any other string gives error A.
addresses.34E9: **TEST-ZERO** (ROM routine): Checks whether the 5-byte number at HL is zero. Carry is set if it is.
addresses.34F9: **greater-0** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $37. Replaces the top number with 1 if it was more than zero, otherwise 0. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3501: **not** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $30. Replaces the top number with 1 if it was zero, otherwise 0, like NOT in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3506: **less-0** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $36. Replaces the top number with 1 if it was below zero, otherwise 0. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.350B: **FP-0/1** (ROM routine): Internal helper that sets the number at HL to 1 if carry is set, or 0 if not. Shared by the true/false operations.
addresses.351B: **no-or-no** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $07. Works like OR in BASIC on the top two numbers: leaves 1 if the second (top) one is not zero, otherwise keeps the first. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3524: **no-&-no** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $08. Works like AND in BASIC on the top two numbers: keeps the first if the second (top) one is not zero, otherwise leaves 0. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.352D: **str-&-no** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $10. BASIC's A$ AND N: keeps the string if the number is not zero, otherwise gives an empty string.
addresses.353B: **compare** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $09 to $0E (numbers) and $11 to $16 (strings). Compares the top two values using <=, >=, <>, >, < or = and leaves 1 for true or 0 for false.
addresses.359C: **strs-add** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $17. Joins two strings together (A$+B$ in BASIC), making a new string in the work space.
addresses.35BF: **STK-PNTRS** (ROM routine): Sets HL to the start of the top number on the calculator stack and DE to just past it (STKEND).
addresses.35C9: **chrs** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2F. Turns the top number into a one-character string with that character code, like CHR$ in BASIC.
addresses.35DE: **val** (ROM routine): Calculator operations $18 (VAL) and $1D (VAL$). Treats a string as a piece of BASIC and works it out, giving a number for VAL or a string for VAL$.
addresses.361F: **str$** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $2E. Turns the top number into a string, exactly as PRINT would show it, like STR$ in BASIC.
addresses.3645: **read-in** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $1A. Reads one character from a given stream and returns it as a string. Seems meant for extra devices beyond the standard Spectrum.
addresses.3669: **code** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $1C. Gives the character code of the first letter of a string, or 0 for an empty string, like CODE in BASIC.
addresses.3674: **len** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $1E. Gives the length of a string, like LEN in BASIC.
addresses.367A: **dec-jr-nz** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $35. Counts down a loop counter kept in BREG and jumps back in the code list if it has not reached zero, like DJNZ for calculator code. Used by the series operation.
addresses.3686: **jump** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $33. Always jumps within the calculator code list, by the offset in the next byte. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.368F: **jump-true** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $00. Jumps within the calculator code list, by the offset in the next byte, if the top number is not zero (true). Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.369B: **end-calc** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $38. Marks the end of a list of calculator codes; your machine code carries on from the byte after it. Every RST $28 list must end with $38.
addresses.36A0: **n-mod-m** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $32. Divides the lower number by the top number, both whole. Leaves the remainder underneath and the whole-number answer on top. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.36AF: **int** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $27. Rounds the top number down to a whole number, like INT in BASIC, so 2.4 gives 2 and -2.4 gives -3. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.36C4: **exp** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $26. Replaces the top number x with e to the power x, like EXP in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3713: **ln** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $25. Replaces the top number with its natural logarithm, like LN in BASIC. Zero or negative numbers give error A. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3783: **get-argt** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $39. Helper for SIN and COS: squeezes an angle into a small range that gives the same answer, so the series can work on it.
addresses.37AA: **cos** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $20. Replaces the top number (an angle in radians) with its cosine, like COS in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.37B5: **sin** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $1F. Replaces the top number (an angle in radians) with its sine, like SIN in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.37DA: **tan** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $21. Replaces the top number (an angle in radians) with its tangent, like TAN in BASIC. Gives an overflow error where tangent has no value. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.37E2: **atn** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $24. Replaces the top number with the angle (in radians) whose tangent it is, like ATN in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3833: **asn** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $22. Replaces the top number with the angle (in radians) whose sine it is, like ASN in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3843: **acs** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $23. Replaces the top number with the angle (in radians) whose cosine it is, like ACS in BASIC. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.384A: **sqr** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $28. Replaces the top number with its square root, like SQR in BASIC. Negative numbers give error A. Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3851: **to-power** (ROM routine): Calculator operation $06. Takes the top two numbers and leaves the first raised to the power of the second (x to the y, like x**y or x^y in BASIC). Normally used through RST $28.
addresses.3D00: **Character set** (ROM table): The ROM's letters and symbols: 96 characters (space to the copyright sign), 8 bytes each, $3D00 to $3FFF. CHARS normally points 256 below it.
addresses.4000: **Screen** (pixels): the first byte of the screen. 6144 bytes, 32 per pixel row, but the rows are not in order: the screen is in three thirds, and within a third, line 1 of every character row comes before line 2. Moving down one pixel inside a character row is INC H.
addresses.5800: **Attributes** (screen colours): one byte for each 8x8 square, 32 per row, 24 rows. Bits 0 to 2 ink, 3 to 5 paper (0 black, 1 blue, 2 red, 3 magenta, 4 green, 5 cyan, 6 yellow, 7 white), bit 6 bright, bit 7 flash.
addresses.5B00: **Printer buffer**: 256 bytes used by the ZX Printer. On a 48K Spectrum without a printer it is free for your own use; 128K Spectrums keep system variables here.
addresses.5B5C: **BANKM** (128K system variable, 23388): a copy of the last value sent to port $7FFD (which can't be read back).
addresses.5C00: **KSTATE** (system variable, 23552): 8 bytes: two sets of 4 bytes that the ROM's keyboard reader uses to track up to two keys being pressed, including the key-repeat timers. Only for the ROM's own use; read LAST-K instead.
addresses.5C04: **KSTATE** (second half, system variable, 23556): the keyboard routine keeps track of up to two keys at once. This byte holds the code of the second key being held, or $FF when there isn't one.
addresses.5C08: **LAST-K** (system variable, 23560): The code of the most recent key pressed, updated by the ROM's keyboard scan 50 times a second when interrupts are on. Handy for simple key reading in machine code: clear bit 5 of FLAGS, wait for it to be set, then read this.
addresses.5C09: **REPDEL** (system variable, 23561): How long a key must be held before it starts repeating, in 50ths of a second (normally 35, about 0.7 s). Poke it to change key repeat speed.
addresses.5C0A: **REPPER** (system variable, 23562): The gap between repeats while a key stays held down, in 50ths of a second (normally 5, so 10 repeats a second).
addresses.5C0B: **DEFADD** (system variable, 23563): 2 bytes: where the values passed to a BASIC DEF FN function are while it is being worked out; 0 otherwise. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C0D: **K-DATA** (system variable, 23565): Keeps the second byte of a colour control (such as INK or PAPER) typed at the keyboard in the editor. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C0E: **TVDATA** (system variable, 23566): 2 bytes: a scratch store for colour, AT and TAB control codes and their first value while they are being printed. Only for the ROM's own use.
addresses.5C10: **STRMS** (system variable, 23568): 38 bytes: 2 bytes for each stream (-3 to 15), saying which channel it is joined to, as an offset into the channel area at CHANS. Changed by OPEN # and CLOSE #.
addresses.5C36: **CHARS** (system variable, 23606): 2 bytes: 256 less than the address of the font used for printing (normally 15360, the font in ROM). Point it at your own 768-byte font, minus 256, to change the lettering.
addresses.5C38: **RASP** (system variable, 23608): How long the warning buzz lasts when the edit line is full or something is wrong (normally 64).
addresses.5C39: **PIP** (system variable, 23609): How long the click is when a key is pressed (normally 0). Poke a bigger value for a louder, longer click.
addresses.5C3A: **ERR-NR** (system variable, 23610): The error report code minus one; 255 (-1) means no error. The IY register normally points here, so the ROM reaches many system variables as IY plus an offset - keep IY unchanged if you use the ROM or interrupts.
addresses.5C3B: **FLAGS** (system variable, 23611): A set of on/off flags used by BASIC. Bit 5 is set when a new key has been pressed (see LAST-K), which machine code often uses to wait for a key; most other bits are for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C3C: **TV-FLAG** (system variable, 23612): On/off flags about the screen, such as whether printing is going to the lower two lines (bit 0) or the lower part needs clearing (bit 5). Mostly for the ROM's own use.
addresses.5C3D: **ERR-SP** (system variable, 23613): 2 bytes: the address on the machine stack that holds where to jump if an error happens. Machine code can change it to catch BASIC errors itself, but take care.
addresses.5C3F: **LIST-SP** (system variable, 23615): 2 bytes: the stack position to go back to after an automatic listing ends. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C41: **MODE** (system variable, 23617): Which kind of cursor the editor shows: 0 for K, L or C, 1 for E, 2 for G (graphics).
addresses.5C42: **NEWPPC** (system variable, 23618): 2 bytes: the BASIC line number to jump to next, such as after GO TO. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C44: **NSPPC** (system variable, 23620): The statement number within the line to jump to; 255 means no jump is waiting. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C45: **PPC** (system variable, 23621): 2 bytes: the line number of the BASIC statement being run right now.
addresses.5C47: **SUBPPC** (system variable, 23623): Which statement within the current BASIC line is being run (1 for the first after the line number).
addresses.5C48: **BORDCR** (system variable, 23624): The border colour (0-7, held in bits 3 to 5) plus the colours for the lower two screen lines. The ROM uses it to restore the border after BEEP, SAVE and LOAD.
addresses.5C49: **E-PPC** (system variable, 23625): 2 bytes: the number of the current BASIC line, the one with the > marker in listings.
addresses.5C4B: **VARS** (system variable, 23627): 2 bytes: where BASIC's variables start in memory, just after the program.
addresses.5C4D: **DEST** (system variable, 23629): 2 bytes: where the variable being given a new value is kept. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C4F: **CHANS** (system variable, 23631): 2 bytes: where the channel table starts (normally 23734). Each entry gives the print and input routines for a channel such as the screen or printer.
addresses.5C51: **CURCHL** (system variable, 23633): 2 bytes: the channel entry being used right now for printing and input. RST 16 prints a character through it, so pick a channel (e.g. call 5633 with A=2 for the main screen) before printing.
addresses.5C53: **PROG** (system variable, 23635): 2 bytes: where the BASIC program starts in memory.
addresses.5C55: **NXTLIN** (system variable, 23637): 2 bytes: where the next line of the BASIC program is. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C57: **DATADD** (system variable, 23639): 2 bytes: where READ will look for its next DATA item. Changed by RESTORE.
addresses.5C59: **E-LINE** (system variable, 23641): 2 bytes: where the line being typed in the editor is stored; it also marks the end of the variables area.
addresses.5C5B: **K-CUR** (system variable, 23643): 2 bytes: where the editing cursor is in the line being typed.
addresses.5C5D: **CH-ADD** (system variable, 23645): 2 bytes: the next character BASIC will look at while reading a line. Only for the ROM's own use.
addresses.5C5F: **X-PTR** (system variable, 23647): 2 bytes: where to show the flashing ? marker after a syntax error. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C61: **WORKSP** (system variable, 23649): 2 bytes: where BASIC's temporary work area starts.
addresses.5C63: **STKBOT** (system variable, 23651): 2 bytes: the bottom of the calculator stack, the area the ROM uses for numbers during sums.
addresses.5C65: **STKEND** (system variable, 23653): 2 bytes: the top of the calculator stack, where free memory begins.
addresses.5C67: **BREG** (system variable, 23655): Used as a spare counter (like a B register) by the ROM's calculator. Only for the ROM's own use.
addresses.5C68: **MEM** (system variable, 23656): 2 bytes: where the calculator's six number stores are (normally MEMBOT).
addresses.5C6A: **FLAGS2** (system variable, 23658): More on/off flags. Bit 3 shows CAPS LOCK is on; bit 1 shows the printer buffer is in use. Mostly for the ROM's own use.
addresses.5C6B: **DF-SZ** (system variable, 23659): How many lines the lower part of the screen uses (normally 2). Setting it to 0 can crash the machine.
addresses.5C6C: **S-TOP** (system variable, 23660): 2 bytes: the line number shown at the top of an automatic listing.
addresses.5C6E: **OLDPPC** (system variable, 23662): 2 bytes: the line number CONTINUE goes back to.
addresses.5C70: **OSPCC** (system variable, 23664): The statement number within the line that CONTINUE goes back to.
addresses.5C71: **FLAGX** (system variable, 23665): More on/off flags, mostly about INPUT and setting variables. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C72: **STRLEN** (system variable, 23666): 2 bytes: the length of a string being given a new value (or a variable's letter in some cases). Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C74: **T-ADDR** (system variable, 23668): 2 bytes: the next item in the ROM's table of BASIC command rules. Only for the ROM's own use (SAVE/LOAD also use it to tell which command was typed).
addresses.5C76: **SEED** (system variable, 23670): 2 bytes: the starting value for RND. Set by RANDOMIZE; changing it gives a different run of random numbers.
addresses.5C78: **FRAMES** (system variable, 23672): 3 bytes: a counter that goes up by 1 every 50th of a second while interrupts are on (lowest byte first). Good for timing and delays in machine code.
addresses.5C7B: **UDG** (system variable, 23675): 2 bytes: the address of the first user-defined graphic, normally 65368 on a 48K machine. Point it elsewhere to switch to another set of 21 custom characters.
addresses.5C7D: **COORDS** (system variable, 23677): 2 bytes: the x then y position of the last point drawn with PLOT, DRAW or CIRCLE.
addresses.5C7F: **P-POSN** (system variable, 23679): The column number where the printer will print next.
addresses.5C80: **PR-CC** (system variable, 23680): 2 bytes: where in the printer buffer LPRINT will put the next character (only the low byte changes).
addresses.5C82: **ECHO-E** (system variable, 23682): 2 bytes: the column and line where the input being typed ends. Only for BASIC's own use.
addresses.5C84: **DF-CC** (system variable, 23684): 2 bytes: the screen memory address where PRINT will put the next character in the main part of the screen.
addresses.5C86: **DF-CCL** (system variable, 23686): 2 bytes: the same as DF-CC, but for the lower part of the screen.
addresses.5C88: **S-POSN** (system variable, 23688): 2 bytes: the PRINT position as column then line, counted down from 33 and 24 (so 33 is the left edge, 24 the top line).
addresses.5C8A: **S-POSNL** (system variable, 23690): 2 bytes: the same as S-POSN, but for the lower part of the screen.
addresses.5C8C: **SCR-CT** (system variable, 23692): Counts lines left before the 'scroll?' question appears. Keep poking it with a value above 1 (e.g. 255) to stop the question.
addresses.5C8D: **ATTR-P** (system variable, 23693): The everyday colours (ink, paper, bright, flash) set by INK, PAPER and so on; used when the screen is cleared. Poke it before CLS to choose screen colours.
addresses.5C8E: **MASK-P** (system variable, 23694): Marks which colour bits should be left as they are on screen (for INK 8, PAPER 8 and the like). Each set bit keeps the screen's own bit.
addresses.5C8F: **ATTR-T** (system variable, 23695): The colours used for the next thing printed. Normally the same as ATTR-P, but changed for a while by colours put inside a PRINT.
addresses.5C90: **MASK-T** (system variable, 23696): Like MASK-P, but for the colours in use just now: set bits keep the colour already on screen, clear bits take it from ATTR-T.
addresses.5C91: **P-FLAG** (system variable, 23697): Printing flags for OVER, INVERSE, INK 9 and PAPER 9. Even bits are the ones in use just now, odd bits are the lasting settings.
addresses.5C92: **MEMBOT** (system variable, 23698): 30 bytes: the calculator's six number stores of 5 bytes each. The ROM also uses this area as scratch space, e.g. for drawing and tape headers.
addresses.5CB0: **NMIADD** (system variable, 23728): 2 bytes: meant to hold an address to jump to when the NMI button signal arrives, but a bug in the 48K ROM means it is only used if it is 0, so it is not useful.
addresses.5CB2: **RAMTOP** (system variable, 23730): 2 bytes: the last byte BASIC may use. Memory above it is safe from BASIC, so machine code usually goes there; CLEAR changes it.
addresses.5CB4: **P-RAMT** (system variable, 23732): 2 bytes: the last byte of memory fitted (65535 on a 48K machine, 32767 on a 16K).
addresses.5CB6: **CHINFO** (system variable, 23734): The start of the channel table, normally just after the system variables. Each channel has 5 bytes: the print routine address, the input routine address and a letter (K, S, R or P); a byte of 128 ends the table.
addresses.8000: The start of the upper 32K. Memory from here up is never slowed down by the screen chip, so it is a favourite place for machine code (ORG 32768).

regions.text: the ROM (BASIC and its routines; it can't be written to)
BASIC's area and free memory, shared with the screen chip (slower while the screen is drawn)
the upper 32K (full speed; on a 128K Spectrum the top 16K, from $C000, is the RAM bank picked with port $7FFD)

ioPorts._about: Hardware reached with IN and OUT. 'anyHigh': the chip answers whatever the top half of the port number is. 'write' and 'readHigh' name decoders in lib/decoders.js.

FE.name: the ULA: border, speaker, keyboard, tape
FE.text: **Port $FE (254)** is the ULA, the Spectrum's main chip. Sending a byte: bits 0 to 2 set the border colour (0 black, 1 blue, 2 red, 3 magenta, 4 green, 5 cyan, 6 yellow, 7 white), bit 3 is the tape output and bit 4 moves the speaker. Reading: the top half of the port number (A, with IN A,($FE)) picks keyboard rows; bits 0 to 4 of the byte read are the keys (0 = pressed) and bit 6 is the tape input.

1F.name: Kempston joystick
1F.text: **Port $1F (31)** is the Kempston joystick interface. Reading it gives bit 0 right, 1 left, 2 down, 3 up, 4 fire (1 = pressed).

7FFD.name: 128K memory paging
7FFD.text: **Port $7FFD** switches memory on 128K Spectrums. Bits 0 to 2 pick the RAM bank seen at $C000, bit 3 shows the second screen (bank 7), bit 4 picks the ROM, bit 5 locks the paging until the next reset. It can't be read back, so programs keep a copy (BANKM, at $5B5C).

FFFD.name: sound chip: pick a register (128K)
FFFD.text: **Port $FFFD** is the AY sound chip on 128K Spectrums. Sending a number 0 to 15 picks which of its registers the next byte sent to $BFFD goes into. Reading gives that register's value.

BFFD.name: sound chip: value (128K)
BFFD.text: **Port $BFFD** is the AY sound chip on 128K Spectrums: the byte sent here goes into the register picked with $FFFD.
